::: {.finding}
Of the committee's {{< meta cfb.cfp_spots >}} at-large picks for the {{< meta cfb.cfp_season >}} playoff, the [power rating](/cfb/tools/team-ratings.html) agrees with {{< meta cfb.cfp_overlap >}}. It would have taken {{< meta cfb.cfp_left_out >}} instead of {{< meta cfb.cfp_instead >}}. In {{< meta cfb.cfp_p_best_out >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_boot >}} resamples of the season, {{< meta cfb.cfp_best_out >}} rates above {{< meta cfb.cfp_worst_pick >}}.
:::

::: {.so-what}
- **Read the seeds as a résumé ranking, not a strength ranking.** In the playoff games of {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_first >}}–{{< meta cfb.cfp_g_last >}}, the higher-rated team won {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_power >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_n >}}; the team the committee ranked higher won {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_committee >}}.
- **When the seed and the rating disagree about a game, lean on the rating.** It was right in {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_dis_power >}} of those {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_dis >}} games (90% interval {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_dis_ci >}}). That's a small sample, so treat it as a lean, not a lock.
- **Don't expect the left-out teams to be long shots.** Every champion since {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_first >}} was in the power rating's top {{< meta cfb.cfp_champ_power_worst >}} at selection, whatever its seed.
:::

## The field and the numbers

```{=html}
<div class="explorer">
  <div class="controls" id="c"></div>
  <div id="field" class="plot-host"></div>
  <p class="caption" id="cap"></p>
</div>
<script>
(async () => {
  const S = Sparvi, f = S.fmt, U = S.urlState;
  const D = await S.load("/data/cfb/cfp_selection.json");
  const all = [...D.history, D.current], bySeason = new Map(all.map(v => [String(v.season), v]));
  const SEASONS = all.map(v => String(v.season)).reverse();
  const DEF = { season: SEASONS[0] };
  const st = { season: bySeason.has(U.get("season")) ? U.get("season") : DEF.season };
  const bub = new Map(D.bubble.map(b => [b.team, b]));
  // One x scale for every season, so seasons compare at a glance.
  const xd = S.stableDomain(all.flatMap(v => v.top.map(t => t.power)), { q: [0, 1] });
  const c = document.getElementById("c"), host = document.getElementById("field");
  function kind(v, t) {
    if (v.left_out.some(x => x.team === t.team)) return "out";
    if (v.chosen_instead.some(x => x.team === t.team)) return "instead";
    return t.in_field ? "in" : "no";
  }
  const FILL = { in: "#0f5257", out: "#eb6834", instead: "#2a78d6", no: "#c9c7c0" };
  function draw() {
    const v = bySeason.get(st.season), cur = +st.season === D.season;
    const auto = new Set(v.rows.filter(r => r.bid === "auto").map(r => r.team));
    const rows = v.top.map(t => ({ ...t, k: kind(v, t), auto: auto.has(t.team),
      label: `${t.team}${t.committee_rank ? ` (${t.committee_rank})` : ""}`, b: cur ? bub.get(t.team) : null }));
    const ivals = rows.filter(r => r.b);
    S.plot(host, w => Plot.plot({ ...S.plotDefaults(w), height: 24 * rows.length + 60, marginLeft: w < 520 ? 118 : 160, marginBottom: 40, clip: true, style: { fontSize: w < 520 ? "10.5px" : "12px" },
      x: { label: w < 520 ? "Power rating (points) →" : "Power rating at selection (points vs. an average FBS team) →", domain: xd, grid: true, ticks: w < 520 ? 4 : 8, labelAnchor: "center", labelOffset: 34 },
      y: { label: null, domain: rows.map(r => r.label), tickSize: 0 },
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY(ivals, { y: "label", x1: d => d.b.lo90, x2: d => d.b.hi90, stroke: "#8a8b8f", strokeWidth: 1.5 }),
        Plot.dot(rows, { x: "power", y: "label", r: 6, fill: d => d.auto ? "#fff" : FILL[d.k], stroke: d => FILL[d.k], strokeWidth: d => d.auto ? 2.5 : 1 }),
        Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointer({ x: "power", y: "label", title: d => `${d.team}: power rating #${d.power_rank} (${f.signed(d.power, 1)})`
          + `\n${d.committee_rank ? `Committee #${d.committee_rank}` : "Unranked by the committee"}`
          + `\n${d.k === "out" ? "Left out; the rating would pick it" : d.k === "instead" ? "At-large pick the rating would leave out" : d.in_field ? (d.auto ? "In the field (automatic bid)" : "In the field (at-large)") : "Not in the field"}`
          + (d.b ? `\n90% range ${f.signed(d.b.lo90, 1)} to ${f.signed(d.b.hi90, 1)}` : "") }))
      ] }));
    U.set({ season: st.season }, DEF);
    document.getElementById("cap").textContent = `${v.season}, ${v.field_size}-team field (committee rank in parentheses), ${cur && !D.final ? "the committee's latest ranking read as if the season ended now" : "as selected"}. `
      + `Teal: in the field (hollow: automatic bid for a conference champion${v.field_size === 4 ? ", none before 2024" : ""}). Orange: left out, though the power rating would take it; blue: the at-large picks it would leave out. `
      + `The rating agrees with ${v.overlap} of ${v.at_large_spots} at-large picks.` + (cur ? " Gray bars: the middle 90% of the resampled ratings." : "");
  }
  c.replaceChildren(S.select("Season", SEASONS.map(s => [s, s]), st.season, v => { st.season = v; draw(); }));
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## How sure is "left out"?

A power rating is an estimate from about a dozen games. To see how much the {{< meta cfb.cfp_season >}} order could move, the season's games were resampled with replacement {{< meta cfb.cfp_boot >}} times and the efficiency half of the rating refit each time. {{< meta cfb.cfp_best_out >}} came out ahead of {{< meta cfb.cfp_worst_pick >}} (the lowest-rated at-large pick, #{{< meta cfb.cfp_worst_pick_rank >}} in the power rating) in {{< meta cfb.cfp_p_best_out >}} of them. Averaged over the resamples, {{< meta cfb.cfp_exp_overlap >}} of the committee's {{< meta cfb.cfp_spots >}} at-large picks rate among the best {{< meta cfb.cfp_spots >}} teams without an automatic bid.

```{=html}
<div id="bubble"><div class="loading">Loading…</div></div>
<p class="caption" id="bcap"></p>
<script>
(async () => {
  const S = Sparvi, f = S.fmt, D = await S.load("/data/cfb/cfp_selection.json");
  const share = v => v > 0.99 ? ">99%" : v < 0.01 ? "<1%" : f.pct(v, 0);   // never round to a certainty
  const t = S.table(document.getElementById("bubble"), [
    { key: "team", label: "Team", align: "l" }, { key: "in_field", label: "Selected", fmt: v => v ? "Yes" : "No" },
    { key: "power", label: "Rating", fmt: v => f.signed(v, 1) },
    { key: "p_top", label: `In top ${D.current.at_large_spots}`, fmt: share },
    { key: "p_above_worst_pick", label: `Above ${D.current.worst_pick}`, fmt: v => v == null ? "(that pick)" : share(v) }],
    { sortKey: "power", desc: true, pageSize: 20 });
  t.update(D.bubble);
  document.getElementById("bcap").textContent = `${D.season}: the best-rated teams without an automatic bid, plus every at-large pick. Shares are of ${D.boot.toLocaleString()} resamples of the season's games: how often each team rated among the best ${D.current.at_large_spots} without an automatic bid, and how often it rated above ${D.current.worst_pick}, the lowest-rated at-large pick.`;
})();
</script>
```

## {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_n >}} seasons of committee picks

The committee doesn't set out to pick the twelve strongest teams. Its protocol weighs conference championships, strength of schedule, head-to-head results, and results against common opponents, and {{< meta cfb.cfp_auto >}} spots go to conference champions by rule. Those automatic bids aren't a judgment call, so the comparison here is the at-large picks only: the committee's against the best-rated teams outside the automatic bids. Across {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_first >}}–{{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_last >}}, the two agreed on {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_overlap >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_spots >}} picks ({{< meta cfb.cfp_h4_overlap >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_h4_spots >}} in the {{< meta cfb.cfp_h4_n >}} four-team seasons, {{< meta cfb.cfp_h12_overlap >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_h12_spots >}} in the {{< meta cfb.cfp_h12_n >}} twelve-team seasons), and matched exactly in {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_exact >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_n >}} seasons.

```{=html}
<div id="hist"><div class="loading">Loading…</div></div>
<p class="caption">Each season's field as selected, against the power rating at selection (after the conference title games). Ranks in parentheses are the power rating's; for the champion, the committee's seed-day rank and then the power rating's. "Agreed": at-large picks the rating would also make.</p>
<script>
(async () => {
  const S = Sparvi, D = await S.load("/data/cfb/cfp_selection.json");
  const list = xs => xs.map(x => `${x.team} (${x.power_rank})`).join(", ");
  const t = S.table(document.getElementById("hist"), [
    { key: "season", label: "Season" },
    { key: "overlap", label: "Agreed", fmt: (v, r) => `${v} of ${r.at_large_spots}` },
    { key: "left_out", label: "Would add", align: "l", fmt: v => list(v) },
    { key: "chosen_instead", label: "Would drop", align: "l", fmt: v => list(v) },
    { key: "champion", label: "Champion", align: "l", fmt: (v, r) => v ? `${v} (${r.champion_committee_rank}, ${r.champion_power_rank})` : "" }],
    { sortKey: "season", desc: true, pageSize: 20 });
  t.update(D.history);
})();
</script>
```

## Does it matter who's seeded where?

Once the bracket is set, the games decide it. Across the {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_n >}} playoff games of {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_first >}}–{{< meta cfb.cfp_g_last >}}, the team rated higher at selection won {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_power >}} and the team the committee ranked higher won {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_committee >}}. The two disagreed about {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_dis >}} of those games, and the rating's pick won {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_dis_power >}}. Every champion in that span was in the rating's top {{< meta cfb.cfp_champ_power_worst >}} when the field was set; {{< meta cfb.cfp_champ_power_top4 >}} of {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_n >}} were in its top four.

<details class="method">
<summary>Method, data, and limits</summary>

**Data.** Games, play-by-play, committee rankings, and pre-game Elo from [CollegeFootballData.com](https://collegefootballdata.com), FBS seasons {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_first >}}–{{< meta cfb.cfp_season >}}.

**The field.** The committee's final ranking of each season. Through {{< meta cfb.cfp_hist_first >}}–{{< meta cfb.cfp_four_last >}} the field was its top four. From {{< meta cfb.cfp_twelve_first >}} it's the {{< meta cfb.cfp_auto >}} highest-ranked conference champions plus the {{< meta cfb.cfp_at_large12 >}} highest-ranked other teams; that rule reproduces every field that has played, team for team.

**The power rating** is the one on the [team ratings tool](/cfb/tools/team-ratings.html): opponent-adjusted EPA per play combined with CFBD's Elo, in points against an average FBS team, as of the conference title games. Its picks are the best-rated teams outside the automatic bids, as many as there are at-large spots. Model version: [{{< meta models.cfb_power_rating >}}](https://github.com/matt-hardman15/sparvi-site/tree/main/models/cfb/power_rating/card.yml) ({{< meta models.cfb_power_rating_status >}}).

**The resampling** draws the season's games with replacement ({{< meta cfb.cfp_boot >}} times, fixed seed) and refits the efficiency half of the rating on the drawn plays. Elo is held at its value, so the ranges are somewhat too narrow.

**What it can't tell you.** The committee is asked to weigh résumés, and a rating of how well a team played is a different question; "the rating disagrees" isn't "the committee erred". The rating's two weights were fit on these same seasons' games, which flatters its record in the playoff games a little. Injuries, quarterback changes, and opt-outs aren't in the numbers. And {{< meta cfb.cfp_g_n >}} playoff games is a small sample.

</details>
